items.title: Adrian Cunningham interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 31, 2021
items.q: Rossano Sportiello said something once to me that really made an impression on me when he was in his late teens learning to play... and I wonder if in Australia is that a goal...

ctx.x: I think trad jazz went in a direction that I think removed some of the foundations of what it was about. I mean Louis Armstrong was such an ambassador for the New Orleans style. And then I think it kind of tends to have lost the — dare I say — the black influence and tended to be just the color of a bunch of white dudes you know, and certainly growing up for me, well I was Australian, not everyone that’s white in Australia plays jazz but you know you go to the festivals and there’s a lot of corny old guys…

It is. Rossano Sportiello said something once to me that really made an impression on me when he was in his late teens learning to play, much like you were I think in clubs and stuff, and if they had a particularly good night he said that would say to one another, “You were wonderful tonight, you sounded American.” And I wonder if in Australia is that a goal or is it not really an issue, to sound American and what would that mean anyway?

That’s a whole other topic of discussion that’s very complex. I think, because it’s tricky isn’t it, because fundamentally this is American music and jazz will always be American. I mean it’s such a huge cultural gift to the world, this music, but of course jazz at the same time it’s malleable. You know you can bring other influences into it. It can be fused © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
